questions.question: What are civil liberties?
choices: Benefits granted only to public officials
Responsibilities of military commanders
Protections for individual freedom against government interference
Powers reserved exclusively for political parties

questions.question: Which amendment protects speech, press, assembly, petition, and religious freedom?
choices: First
Fourth
Sixth
Tenth

questions.question: Which constitutional protection concerns unreasonable government searches and seizures?
choices: Seventh Amendment
Third Amendment
Ninth Amendment
Fourth Amendment

questions.question: Which amendment includes a protection against compelled self-incrimination?
choices: Second
Fifth
Eighth
Tenth

questions.question: Which amendment protects the right to assistance of counsel in criminal prosecutions?
choices: Sixth
Third
Seventh
Ninth

questions.question: What is prior restraint in a freedom-of-expression dispute?
choices: A penalty imposed after a publication is found unlawful
A private reader's decision not to purchase a newspaper
Government action preventing expression before it occurs
A publisher's voluntary correction of an inaccurate report

questions.question: What does the Free Exercise Clause concern?
choices: Congress's power to regulate interstate commerce
A governor's authority to set tax rates
A court's authority to schedule trials
Protection of religious belief and practice

questions.question: What is the basic purpose of the Establishment Clause?
choices: To select one national religious leader
To limit government establishment of religion
To require citizens to join a religious organization
To remove religious speech from private homes

questions.question: Why is criticism of public officials an important protected form of speech?
choices: It helps people debate policy and hold government accountable
It guarantees critics will win every election
It removes the need for evidence in public discussion
It gives critics immunity from every generally applicable law

questions.question: How has the Fourteenth Amendment affected many Bill of Rights protections?
choices: It repealed all protections involving criminal trials
It restricted them to residents of the national capital
It has helped apply many protections to state and local governments
It made those protections optional for each state legislature

questions.question: Why does the Fourth Amendment not prohibit every government search?
choices: It applies only when a suspect admits guilt
It protects property but never people
It gives police unlimited authority inside homes
It prohibits unreasonable searches rather than all searches

questions.question: What is the purpose of due process protections?
choices: To guarantee that every accused person is acquitted
To require fair procedures before government deprives a person of protected interests
To let officials punish people without a hearing
To transfer every criminal case to the legislature

questions.question: Why is the right to peaceful assembly important in civic life?
choices: It allows people to gather and express shared concerns
It authorizes private groups to replace elected governments
It permits participants to disregard all safety rules
It guarantees that officials must adopt every protest demand

questions.question: What does freedom of the press protect most directly?
choices: A publisher's right to receive guaranteed government profits
An editor's authority to appoint public officials
The ability to publish information and opinions without improper government suppression
A newspaper's exemption from every civil lawsuit

questions.question: Why can courts face difficult questions involving civil liberties?
choices: Constitutional text eliminates every disagreement
Civil liberties apply only when everyone agrees
Courts cannot interpret any constitutional provision
Individual freedoms may interact with other rights and public interests

questions.question: A city denies a peaceful group's park permit solely because officials dislike its message. Which concern is most directly raised?
choices: A change in congressional apportionment
Viewpoint discrimination against protected expression
A conflict over military command
A dispute over state boundary lines

questions.question: A government forces an accused person to testify against themselves in a criminal case. Which protection is directly implicated?
choices: The Fifth Amendment's self-incrimination protection
The Third Amendment's quartering restriction
The Seventh Amendment's civil-jury protection
The Tenth Amendment's reservation of powers

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes a civil liberty from a guaranteed favorable outcome?
choices: Freedom of speech guarantees public agreement
The right to counsel guarantees acquittal
Protected participation does not guarantee that one's preferred policy will be adopted
Freedom of the press guarantees that every report is accurate

questions.question: A state prosecutes a person under its own criminal laws. Why might federal constitutional protections still matter?
choices: State courts are exempt from every constitutional requirement
Only federal officials can investigate crimes
State legislation automatically overrides constitutional rights
Many federal rights also constrain state government through incorporation

questions.question: A private club disagrees with a member's opinion. What fact should be checked before treating the dispute as a First Amendment violation?
choices: Whether the opinion is popular with all club members
Whether the challenged action involves government rather than only private conduct
Whether the speaker has voted in every election
Whether the club uses printed rather than digital messages
